residencyRequirements.description: At least one spouse must have been a domiciliary of Texas for the preceding six-month period and a resident of the county for the preceding ninety-day period.

exceptions.description: Spouse convicted of or received deferred adjudication for family violence
Active protective order or magistrate's order for emergency protection due to family violence

noFault.name: Insupportability
noFault.description: Discord or conflict of personalities that destroys the legitimate ends of the marriage

fault.name: Cruel Treatment
fault.description: Treatment of such nature as to render further living together insupportable

fault.name: Conviction of Felony
fault.description: Spouse convicted of felony and imprisoned for at least one year without pardon

fault.name: Abandonment
fault.description: Spouse left with intention of abandonment and remained away at least one year

fault.name: Living Apart
fault.description: Spouses lived apart without cohabitation for at least three years

fault.name: Confinement in Mental Hospital
fault.description: Spouse confined in mental hospital for at least three years with unlikely recovery

propertyDivision.description: Texas is a community property state. Property acquired during marriage is presumed community property and is subject to a just and right division by the court. Separate property includes property owned before marriage or acquired during marriage by gift, devise, or descent.

service.name: Waiver of Service
service.notes: Must be signed at least one day after petition filed, must be notarized

withChildren.name: Standing Order
withChildren.description: Automatic restraining orders regarding children and property

withChildren.name: Income Withholding Order
withChildren.description: Order for employer to withhold child support

withChildren.name: Medical Support Order
withChildren.description: Health and dental insurance for children

formattingRequirements.notes: Per Texas Rules of Civil Procedure

filingFees.notes: Varies by county. Fee waiver available for indigent parties via Statement of Inability to Afford Payment of Court Costs (Tex. R. Civ. P. 145).

inState.description: Respondent must file an answer by 10:00 a.m. on the first Monday after 20 days have passed since service. If the 20th day falls on a Monday, the answer is due the following Monday.

outOfState.description: Same rule applies — answer due by 10:00 a.m. on the first Monday after 20 days from service

childSupportGuidelines.incomeCapNote: Applies to first $11,700/month of net resources (effective September 1, 2025)

requirements: Spouse lacks ability to earn sufficient income
Spouse is custodian of child with disability requiring substantial care
Family violence within 2 years of filing
spousalMaintenanceEligibility.maximumAmount: Lesser of $5,000/month or 20% of obligor's gross income
